questions.question: Describe the role of a constitution in a democratic system.
questions.solution_html:
• Constitution in a democratic system sets the framework for governance, defines powers
  • and duties of institutions, guarantees citizens’ rights, and ensures rule of law-it acts as the
  • supreme legal authority guiding democratic functioning, accountability, and protection of
  • individual freedoms.

questions.question: What were the main criticisms against the Government of India Act / 1935?
questions.solution_html:
• Government of India Act 1935 was criticized for being complex, retaining British control
  • denying full autonomy, and excluding Indian representation in key decisions-lack of real
  • federalism-did not address the issues of fundamental rights-continuing British control over
  • defence and foreign affairs- centralized power and failed to reflect democratic principles
  • making it unacceptable to nationalists and Indian political leaders.
questions.final_answer: making it unacceptable to nationalists and Indian political leaders

questions.question: Examine the role of the Indian National Congress in shaping / constitutional ideas in India.
questions.solution_html:
• Indian National Congress influenced constitutional development by demanding
  • responsible government and promoting civil liberties-Nehru Report, 1928 proposed a
  • constitutional framework for India -1931 Karachi Resolution- democratic values, inclusive
  • nationalism, secularism, fundamental rights, socio-economic reforms and representative
  • institutions, laying the ideological groundwork for the Constitution adopted post
  • independence.

questions.question: What are the criticisms of the Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution_html:
• Criticisms of Fundamental Rights include excessive limitations, vague language, and
  • dependence on judicial interpretation-they are criticized for focusing primarily on political
  • rights while neglecting social and economic rights-some rights are not absolute and can be
  • suspended, especially during emergencies, reducing their effectiveness in protecting
  • individual freedoms in all situations.

questions.question: How does the Preamble reflect the aspirations of the people of India?
questions.solution_html:
• Preamble expresses India’s commitment to justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity-it
  • reflects the people's aspirations for a sovereign, democratic, secular, and inclusive society and
  • serves as a guiding principle for interpreting the Constitution and ensuring social and political
  • ideals.

questions.question: Does the executive’s control over law-making weaken parliamentary / democracy? “The opposition is not to oppose, but to propose.” How far is
questions.solution_html:
• Excessive executive influence over legislation, through party majority and control over
  • parliamentary agenda, can weaken legislative scrutiny and reduce debate quality, potentially
  • undermining the independence and effectiveness of parliamentary democracy in holding the
  • government accountable-the legislature is intended to scrutinize and debate the executive's
  • proposals-the use of presidential ordinances in India, which are executive decrees that have
  • the force of law, has been criticized for undermining the role of parliament in law-making .
questions.final_answer: the force of law, has been criticized for undermining the role of parliament in law-making

questions.question: / this true in the Indian parliamentary system?
questions.solution_html:
• Opposition is expected to offer constructive criticism and policy alternatives, not just
  • disrupt proceeding-though often adversarial, its role is vital for democratic balance, legislative
  • improvement, and checking the ruling party, ensuring accountability and diverse
  • perspectives in governance-opposition serves to make the ruling party accountable for their
  • actions, reminding them that they need to be responsive to the public's needs and concerns.
questions.final_answer: actions, reminding them that they need to be responsive to the public's needs and concerns

questions.question: How has the effectiveness of parliamentary debates changed over / time?
questions.solution_html:
• The effectiveness of parliamentary debates has evolved over time- moving from primarily
  • formal discussions to more engaging and interactive formats with increased opportunities for
  • members to express their views and hold the executive accountable-parliamentary debates
  • have also declined in quality due to reduced sittings, politicization, frequent disruptions, and
  • lack of informed discussion- traditional debate has a long history, contemporary practices aim
  • to enhance the participation of members and ensure greater accountability of the government
  • while some critical issues are still debated meaningfully, the overall decline hampers
  • transparency, legislative depth, and democratic engagement over time.
questions.final_answer: transparency, legislative depth, and democratic engagement over time

questions.question: What are the financial powers of the Governor?
questions.solution_html:
• Governor’s financial powers include laying the annual state budget before the legislature
  • giving assent to money bills, ensuring the proper procedures for budget and expenditure are
  • followed-making certain grants as needed-according to article 203 and 204 of the Indian
  • Constitution- recommending President’s rule in case of financial instability-however, these
  • powers are largely exercised based on the advice of the state’s council of ministers.
questions.final_answer: powers are largely exercised based on the advice of the state’s council of ministers

questions.question: What are the legal provisions under which PIL can be filed in India?
questions.solution_html:
• Public Interest Litigation (PIL) can be filed under Article 32 in the Supreme Court and
  • Article 226 in High Courts-it allows individuals or groups to seek judicial redress in matters
  • affecting public interest, especially for rights violations of disadvantaged groups-the court can
  • take cognizance of a letter or postcard and convert it into a PIL, as seen in the case of Rural
  • Litigation & Entitlement Kendra, Dehradun vs. State of Uttar Pradesh.
questions.final_answer: Litigation & Entitlement Kendra, Dehradun vs. State of Uttar Pradesh

questions.question: Critically evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of the Constituent / Assembly’s working methods.
questions.solution_html:
• Constituent Assembly worked with vision and inclusivity, drawing from global examples
  • and ensuring detailed debates-its strengths included democratic functioning, consensus
  • building, and representation-however, weaknesses included limited representation of some
  • groups, dominance of Congress leaders, and lack of direct elections, which raised concerns
  • about broader public participation.

questions.question: Describe the major categories of Directive Principles and their / objectives.
questions.solution_html:
• Directive Principles are categorized into socialistic (e.g., right to work, education)
  • Gandhian (e.g., village panchayats), and liberal-intellectual (e.g., uniform civil code)-their
  • objectives are to promote social justice, reduce inequality, and guide governance toward a
  • welfare state, even though they are non-justiciable and not legally enforceable.
questions.final_answer: welfare state, even though they are non-justiciable and not legally enforceable

questions.question: Explain the structure and composition of the Rajya Sabha.
questions.solution_html:
• Rajya Sabha, the upper house of Parliament, consists of(245 mark)embers—233 elected by state
  • legislatures and 12 nominated by the President-it represents states, ensures federal balance
  • and reviews legislation-it is a permanent body with one-third of members retiring every two
  • years, ensuring continuity and experience.

questions.question: Evaluate the effectiveness of the writ jurisdiction in protecting citizens’ / rights.
questions.solution_html:
• Writ jurisdiction under Articles 32 and 226 empowers courts to issue writs like habeas
  • corpus, mandamus, and certiorari-it protects fundamental rights and ensures accountability
  • of public authorities-while effective in many cases, delays, judicial backlog, and accessibility
  • issues can limit its real-time effectiveness for ordinary citizens.
questions.final_answer: issues can limit its real-time effectiveness for ordinary citizens

  • Indians to join executive councils for the first time - aimed to involve Indians in
  • administration while maintaining British control over governance.

  • emphasize uniform civil code environmental protection and international peace
  • objective is to guide government in establishing social economic and political
  • democracy in India.

  • central and provincial levels and allowed indirect election of members - introduced
  • separate electorates for Muslims- encouraged communal representation - permitted
  • Indians to join executive councils for the first time - aimed to involve Indians in
  • administration while maintaining British control over governance.
questions.final_answer: administration while maintaining British control over governance

questions.question: Describe the major categories of Directive Principles and their objectives.
questions.solution_html:
• Directive Principles of State Policy are classified into socialist Gandhian and liberal
  • intellectual principles - socialist principles promote welfare state equal justice and
  • reduction of inequalities in society - Gandhian principles encourage village
  • panchayats cottage industries and upliftment of weaker sections - liberal principles
  • emphasize uniform civil code environmental protection and international peace
  • objective is to guide government in establishing social economic and political
  • democracy in India.

questions.question: How does the Prime Minister influence policy-making in India?
questions.solution_html:
• Prime Minister plays central role in policy making as head of government and leader
  • of Council of Ministers - guides formulation and implementation of national policies
  • on economy defence foreign affairs and welfare - coordinates activities of ministries
  • and influences legislative agenda in Parliament - chairs important committees and
  • advises President on major decisions - leadership political support and administrative
  • control make Prime Minister highly influential in governance and decision making.
questions.final_answer: control make Prime Minister highly influential in governance and decision making

questions.question: What are the key features of an independent and impartial judiciary?
questions.solution_html:
• Independent and impartial judiciary ensures fair justice without interference from
  • executive or legislature - judges are provided security of tenure fixed salaries and
  • protection from arbitrary removal - judiciary has power of judicial review to safeguard
  • Constitution and fundamental rights -power of contempt of court- courts function
  • according to rule of law equality and natural justice principles - impartial judiciary
  • strengthens democracy protects citizens liberties and maintains public confidence in
  • legal system.
